key_facts: Ukrainian drones hit Russia's biggest data centre, Sberbank's Balakovo site, on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026
It followed three attacks in the past week on data centres owned by Yandex
Sberbank First Deputy CEO Alexander Vedyakhin confirmed the attack and said all systems operate normally
Yandex's hit centres hosted all three of its operating supercomputers; neither company says whether supercomputers were damaged
The Sberbank site is reported to host Russia's biggest supercomputer, due to start in 2027
Both Sberbank and Yandex say they trail US and Chinese AI leaders by up to nine months, partly due to sanctions on advanced chips
Putin held an unannounced meeting on information security that the Kremlin said was not linked to the attacks
quote_evidence: Ukrainian drones hit Russia's biggest data center on Wednesday, part of a series of attacks appearing to target Moscow's ambitions to develop Russian artificial intelligence capabilities on a par with those from the U.S. and China.

"We confirm that the data processing center was attacked. At the same time, all of Sberbank's systems and services are operating normally and without disruption," Sberbank First Deputy CEO Alexander Vedyakhin told reporters.
why_it_matters_hint: AI computing sites are becoming targets in the war.
notes: Reuters link blocked; same Reuters text read on KSL and CNA.
title: Ukrainian drones hit Russia's top data centre in attack on AI ambitions
